Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT n. 28 s. 09 June 2009 MS. ALMA G. MARFIL MPDC, Municipality of Sibalom Province of Antique Dear Ms. Marfil: This has reference to your earlier letter asking our legal opinion on the following queries, which we quoted in toto: "(1) In the event tha t the SB (Sangguniang Bayan) was not able to 01 erride the veto of the mayor of the development fimd, can the LGU re-enact the 2007 development fund and the corresponding progranls reflected therein which were proposed to be continued for 2008P In case re-enactment is not possible, will a new Annual (g) Development/ investment Plan (MP) for 2008 be submitted to the SBP Or the MDC can re-submit it (sic) the same as the SB failed to return the AIP with their (SB) recommendations but made some insertions and changes in appropriations för prograJns without consultation with the MDCP (S) Can the SB set Ihnita tions on th e u tiliza tion of the development fund, as set forth in Sections II, III, IV of Appropriation Ordinance No. g, series 2008. Will these sections be binding since it was not vetoed by the mayor?" In reply to your first query, may we invite your attention to Section 55 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), thus:

-2- "Section 55. Veto Power of the Local Chief (a) The local chief executive may veto any Executi ve. ordinance of the sanggunian panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, or sanggunian bayan on the ground that it is ultra vires or prejudicial to the public welfare, stating his reasons therefor in writing. (b) The local chief executive, except the punong barangay, shall have the power to veto any particular item or items Of an appropriations ordinance, an ordinance or resolution adopting a local development plan and public investment program, or an ordinance directing the payment of money or creating liability. In such a case, the veto shall not affect the item or items which are not objected to. The vetoed item or items shall not take effect unless the sangænian overrides the veto in the manner herein provided; otherwise, the item or items in the appropriations ordinance of the previous year corresponding to those vetoed, if anyt shall be deemed reenacted. (c) The local chief executive may veto an ordinance or resolution only once. The sanggunian may override the veto of the local chief executive concerned by two-thirds (2/3) vote Of all its members, thereby making the ordinance effective even without the approval of the local chief executive concerned." (Emphasis Supplied) Paragraph (b) of the aforequoted provision simply advances the rule that when the Local Chief Executive exercises his line veto power in an enacted Annual Appropriations Ordinance, those items subject of his line veto are simply left for naught. However, the Sanggunian concerned may override the line veto by garnering a 2/3 vote of all its members and when they had successfully override the same, it is the veto this time which is left dead thereby making the vetoed items deemed approved by the Local Chief Executive. If, on the other hand, the veto is not successfully overridden by the Sanggunian concerned, the item/s in the Annual Appropriations Ordinance of the previous year corresponding to those vetoed shall be deemed reenacted, meaning by operation of law. Please take note that, in your case, the phrase "Annual Appropriations of the previous year" definitely refers to the duly approved Appropriation Ordinance for the fiscal year 2007 and not the proposed Annual Appropriation for fiscal year 2008 submitted to the Local Chief Executive for approval.

-3- Your second query is already rendered irrelevant considering that, as stated above, reenactment of the item/s in the Annual Appropriations Ordinance of the previous year corresponding to those vetoed will be effected by operation of law in the event that the Sangguniang Bayan did not override the veto of your Municipal Mayor. Anent your third query, we are of the view that the limitations on the utilization of the 20% development fund as set forth in Sections II, III and IV of the Appropriations Ordinance No. 02, series of 2008 are just in order considering that they pertain to procedures on how to ensure that the funds were disbursed in accordance with the intended project or program. Along this line, may we point out that since your Municipal Mayor has not vetoed the foregoing sections, the same are thus considered approved. Once approved, these sections are already effective and can be given force and effect even under review by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, subject however to any findings of invalidity by the said August Body. However, in the event that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, in exercising its power of review finds the subject ordinance in accordance with law and pertinent rules, or that the subject ordinance is presumed valid due to inaction by that August Body within thirty (30) days after submission, your remedy therefore is to question the validity of the subject Appropriations Ordinance by filing an appropriate action in court. We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. V truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretar V 1 Regional Director Evelyn A. Trompeta, CEO DILG-Region VI Fort San Pedro, Iloilo City Provincial Director Rosario F. Maza DILG-Antique Legal/20:17
